mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -30.6% to -27.7%, indicates a slow but consistent recovery in discretionary out-of-home activity, which is expected to continue over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility, even from its current low levels, signals a broader return to public transportation for commuting and other activities, directly translating to increased footfall for retail and recreation over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the two weeks following a week where TRANSIT mobility rose by more than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: A combined shift where RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases while WORKPLACES mobility stabilizes or slightly increases indicates a population spending less time at home and more time in public or work-related settings, which will drive an increase in retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point week-on-week while WORKPLACES changes by less than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling and WORKPLACES mobility stabilizing or rising.

mechanism_narrative: The recent surge in PARKS mobility, reaching 28.3% above baseline, suggests favorable weather conditions and increased outdoor leisure activity. This heightened comfort with out-of-home activities will spill over into retail and recreation, boosting mobility within the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility decreases in the week following a period where PARKS mobility was above 25.0.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility directly correlates with reduced out-of-home activity. A significant and sustained drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility below its recent baseline indicates people are spending less time at home, freeing them up for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even if RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 8.0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, indicating increased comfort with essential out-of-home trips, combined with a continued low level of WORKPLACES mobility, suggests that people are venturing out more for non-work reasons, which will eventually translate to higher retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES remains below -35.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM rising for two consecutive weeks and WORKPLACES remaining below -35.0.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent slight recovery in RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT mobility, alongside a recent dip in RESIDENTIAL mobility, collectively signals a broader societal shift towards easing restrictions and increased public confidence in out-of-home activities, driving further retail recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite the observed trends in TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent and significantly low WORKPLACES mobility, consistently below -35% from baseline, indicates that a substantial portion of the workforce continues to operate remotely. This sustained lack of daily commuting and associated foot traffic will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -35.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase (more than 5 points) over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES mobility remains below -35.0 for two consecutive weeks.
